name: s001
text: Google Cloud revenue doubled, yet the stock fell over 10 percent after hours.

name: s002
text: Alphabet's earnings show search queries at a five-year growth high, but search revenue still missed.

name: s003
text: Capital spending hit 51.4 billion dollars, pushing free cash flow to negative 9.1 billion.

name: s004
text: No buybacks, and 12.4 billion dollars of new shares instead.

name: s005
text: Microsoft and Amazon are doing the same, so every AI stock holder should care.

name: s006
text: One-time hit, or real trouble in the core business?

name: s007
text: First, let's clear out the noise. Alphabet earned 2 dollars and 12 cents a share.

name: s008
text: Wall Street expected about 3 dollars. That's roughly 30 percent short.

name: s009
text: The biggest drag wasn't the core business.

name: s010
text: Alphabet's CFO said its stake in SpaceX fell in value this quarter, so it booked a paper loss.

name: s011
text: No cash left the building, so the market usually looks past that.

name: s012
text: But even without it, the core business fell short. Operating income was 40.6 billion dollars, about 6 percent below estimates.

name: s013
text: Operating margin was 31.8 percent, down two points from the second quarter.

name: s014
text: Where did the money go? R&D spending rose 36 percent, driven by AI talent and depreciation.

name: s015
text: The cost of the TPU hardware it sells is pushing costs up too.

name: s016
text: My take: the market can forgive the drop in earnings per share.

name: s017
text: It won't let a miss in core profit slide so easily.

name: s018
text: So why wasn't core profit enough? Start with Google's biggest cash machine.

name: s019
text: Search revenue was 63.4 billion dollars, up 12 percent. Wall Street expected about 65 billion.

name: s020
text: Bank of America's pre-earnings forecast had growth at 14 percent.

name: s021
text: YouTube ads brought in 11.2 billion dollars, up 9.2 percent. That missed too.

name: s022
text: Together that's 74.5 billion dollars, nearly 60 percent of Alphabet's revenue.

name: s023
text: Oddly, people aren't searching less. Sundar Pichai said search query growth was the highest in five years.

name: s024
text: The Gemini app has reached a billion users.

name: s025
text: So why didn't the money follow? Management gave three reasons on the call.

name: s026
text: One, currency. Two, a tough comparison with last year, worth about 3 points of drag.

name: s027
text: Three, AI Mode, the chat-style AI inside search. Usage is growing fast, but it earns less than classic search.

name: s028
text: The third one matters most. Pew Research looked at this last year.

name: s029
text: When a page showed an AI summary, users clicked a regular search result in 8 percent of visits.

name: s030
text: Without the summary, it was 15 percent.

name: s031
text: Fewer clicks out may also mean fewer chances for ads to earn.

name: s032
text: My read: AI isn't making people use Google less. It's making each search earn less.

name: s033
text: Currency and tough comparisons will pass. AI Mode's monetization problem won't fix itself.

name: s034
text: If you're tracking earnings from the big AI names too, subscribe.

name: s035
text: I'm running the numbers on all of them this season.

name: s036
text: The old engine is slowing.

name: s037
text: So why couldn't Google Cloud, the engine that's supposed to take over, hold the stock up?

name: s038
text: Google Cloud brought in 30.7 billion dollars this quarter, up 103 percent.

name: s039
text: Operating income was 11.1 billion dollars, and the margin jumped from 23.7 to 36.2 percent.

name: s040
text: Wall Street expected about 29.1 billion, growth in the low 90s.

name: s041
text: Bank of America was more bullish at 93 percent. So cloud clearly beat.

name: s042
text: So why didn't that help? Do the math.

name: s043
text: Cloud came in 1.6 billion dollars above estimates.

name: s044
text: Search and YouTube together came in 1.8 billion below.

name: s045
text: Net it out, and total revenue still missed slightly.

name: s046
text: The problem is size. Those two ad businesses made 74.5 billion dollars this quarter. Cloud made 30.7 billion.

name: s047
text: For every point of growth ads lose, cloud has to add about 2.4 points to make it up.

name: s048
text: Demand isn't the problem. In September, Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said

name: s049
text: more than 300 customers had each committed over 100 million dollars.

name: s050
text: The cloud backlog hit 561 billion dollars.

name: s051
text: The CFO expects just over half of it to turn into revenue in the next two years.

name: s052
text: Take that margin with a grain of salt, though. The 36 percent doesn't include the cost of building AI models.

name: s053
text: Alphabet books that at the corporate level, and that loss widened from 4.5 billion dollars a year ago to 7.7 billion.

name: s054
text: Management also said it's short on its own computing capacity.

name: s055
text: It started renting third-party compute late in the quarter and will rent more in the fourth.

name: s056
text: Cloud margins will feel it in the near term.

name: s057
text: My take: cloud really is sprinting. It just can't carry all of Google yet.

name: s058
text: On the revenue side, the old engine is slowing and the new one can't make up the gap.

name: s059
text: What about spending? That brings us to the ugliest page in this report: the cash flow statement.

name: s060
text: Alphabet spent 51.4 billion dollars on capital expenditures this quarter. That's double last year, and about 40 percent of revenue.

name: s061
text: Operating cash flow was only 42.3 billion dollars, more than 11 billion below estimates.

name: s062
text: More went out than came in, so free cash flow was negative 9.1 billion dollars.

name: s063
text: A year ago it was positive 24.5 billion.

name: s064
text: Last quarter it was negative 5.9 billion. That's two negative quarters in a row.

name: s065
text: That 11-billion-dollar shortfall in operating cash flow has two pieces worth separating.

name: s066
text: One is a one-off. The CFO said Alphabet paid a 2018 EU fine this quarter, 5.2 billion dollars.

name: s067
text: The other is TPU inventory. Google builds TPU systems first and gets paid on delivery.

name: s068
text: Inventory went from 2.4 billion dollars at the end of last year to 13.3 billion.

name: s069
text: The CFO said all of that inventory is tied to signed contracts.

name: s070
text: So this quarter's cash flow looks worse than normal.

name: s071
text: But the trend of spending more than it earns hasn't changed.

name: s072
text: How does it fill the gap? Alphabet issued about 12.4 billion dollars in new shares through an at-the-market offering.

name: s073
text: It raised 28.7 billion dollars in debt and bought back zero stock.

name: s074
text: It still has 27.6 billion dollars left under that offering program.

name: s075
text: Alphabet isn't short of money. It holds 265 billion dollars in cash and marketable securities.

name: s076
text: Subtract long-term debt, and there's still about 140 billion dollars in net cash.

name: s077
text: But for shareholders, the change is real. The share count used to shrink because profits went into buybacks.

name: s078
text: Now debt and new shares are funding the spending, and the share count is growing.

name: s079
text: My read: some of this quarter is one-off, but spending more than it earns is going to continue.

name: s080
text: Alphabet still has 140 billion dollars in net cash. So why is the market cutting its valuation right now?

name: s081
text: This year's capex guidance is unchanged at 195 to 205 billion dollars.

name: s082
text: That means the fourth quarter alone needs 63 to 73 billion, more than the third.

name: s083
text: And next year? The CFO only said capex will "increase significantly," with details on the next call.

name: s084
text: Bank of America estimates around 300 billion dollars. Morgan Stanley put it near 250 billion back in July.

name: s085
text: Run Bank of America's number. Over the past 12 months, operating cash flow was about 180 billion dollars.

name: s086
text: Now spend 300 billion next year.

name: s087
text: Just to break even on free cash flow, operating cash flow would need to grow nearly 70 percent.

name: s088
text: And that's only next year. On the call, the CFO disclosed 924 billion dollars in future purchase commitments.

name: s089
text: Once signed, those have to be paid.

name: s090
text: On the other side is the 561 billion dollar backlog from customers.

name: s091
text: But the two don't match. Purchase commitments are fixed.

name: s092
text: Whether the backlog turns into cash depends on the customers.

name: s093
text: Some of those customers are AI companies like Anthropic, which are still burning cash themselves.

name: s094
text: If they keep raising money, Google gets paid on time.

name: s095
text: If funding dries up, that risk lands on Google.

name: s096
text: That's why the way the market values Google is shifting.

name: s097
text: Investors used to see a high-margin, cash-rich platform that bought back stock every year.

name: s098
text: Now it looks more like a capital-heavy AI infrastructure company,

name: s099
text: and the market pays a lower multiple for the same profit.

name: s100
text: That 140 billion in net cash shows Google can pay its bills.

name: s101
text: What Wall Street is cutting is how much it will pay for each dollar of profit.

name: s102
text: From here, it can go two ways.

name: s103
text: If AI monetization in search catches up, and TPUs ship on time and turn inventory into cash,

name: s104
text: the market will pay for growth again.

name: s105
text: If those signals keep slipping, analysts will have to cut profit estimates, and today's price may not be the floor.

name: s106
text: My take: there's real value in Google at this price. But I'm waiting for those two signals first.

name: s107
text: To sum up: this drop came from revenue and spending moving the wrong way at the same time.

name: s108
text: Each search earns less, cloud can't fill the gap, and spending keeps speeding up.

name: s109
text: If you own Google, or any big tech name pouring money into AI, here are the three things I'm watching.

name: s110
text: One, the 2027 capex number on the fourth-quarter call.

name: s111
text: Two, whether search growth comes back once AI Mode carries more ads.

name: s112
text: Three, whether TPU deliveries bring that inventory down.

name: s113
text: After this drop, is Google an opportunity or a trap? Tell me in the comments.

name: s114
text: Disclaimer: This video is for information only and is not investment advice.
